> Continue the saved OS and disk. Add a tiny guest-side AArch64 assembler invoked by the shell command asm NAME. Read the source from the named file on the persistent disk and emit real AArch64 machine instructions into the existing program-load buffer, so the existing run command executes them. Preserve earlier functionality. No host assemblers, outside references, or other binaries.
> 
> Support semicolon-separated statements, labels like done: as standalone statements, and these instructions (implicit w0): mov N (decimal 0..65535), add N and sub N (0..4095), b LABEL, ret. Support forward labels, at most eight instructions and source within the existing file size. A successful assembly prints "assembled\n"; malformed source or an unresolved label prints "assembly error\n" and leaves the previous loaded program intact. Report missing source as "not found\n" and absent disk as "no disk\n". Update help. Test a forward branch skipping an instruction, arithmetic and return, and preservation after invalid source. Use fresh file names if possible, stop the VM, and save the image and updated handoff notes within the tool's 8192-character limit.
